author: clothes-dressing-packing designer
description: Washing on lines. Clue `W/gaps/digits`: W = the exact width of the picture (26-30); `gaps` = one digit per LINE, the number of rows of air hanging under that line (3-4 lines, each 2-6, total 6-11); `digits` = one digit per line EXCEPT the last (0-3). Solution: an ASCII drying rack, W columns wide - rows that consist only of '=' and 'v' are lines (pegs are cosmetic 'v's), every other row is air with garments drawn as blocks of one capital letter; a garment is a horizontal run of one letter that hangs from the line above (it must occupy the top row of its block and the same run in every row down to its hem, so garments are rectangles) and each line carries >= 2 garments. THE RULE (private): for each line except the last, count the garments hanging from it that (a) hang all the way down to the line below - their hem touches it - AND (b) have at least one garment hanging directly underneath them from that next line (their columns overlap). 'How many things on this line are dripping on the washing below.' That per-line count must equal the clue's digit for that line. Nothing else is constrained: letters, widths, hems, pegs, filler char and the number of garments are all free. DISCOVERY PATH: one demo gives 'washing hanging on lines'; the picture grammar is rebuilt from 1-2 demos; the whole difficulty is what the digits count. The two rivals a step away - 'the ones that reach the line below' and 'the ones with something underneath' - are BOTH falsified on EVERY line of EVERY shipped demo (generate/solve reject any picture unless reach > digit and below > digit on every line), so demos alone show that the answer is the conjunction. Also rejected in every demo: counting drip PAIRS instead of garments, counting the wet garments below, containment instead of overlap, garments per line, short garments, wide garments, long-and-wide, long-and-narrow, and inner-only variants. MEASURED (600 clues, attackers that know the grammar and build a legal rack satisfying their own law): true rule 100%, count drip pairs 93% and count the wet ones below 88% (synonyms of the same insight, deliberately left paying), 'the ones that reach' 8%, 'the ones with something below' 6%, 'the d widest are the long ones' 19%, long-and-wide 17%, d garments per line 2%, all-long 1%, none-long 0%, random legal rack 6%, previous answer replayed 0.3%, one fixed answer 0.7%, junk/empty 0%. ~5900 distinct clue classes, so brute-force-and-cache over 6 rounds is worth about the 6% floor. Author: clothes/dressing/packing direction.
solve:
WID = [1, 1, 1, 2, 2, 3, 3]


def over(a, b):
    return a[0] < b[0] + b[1] and b[0] < a[0] + a[1]


def block(r, W, hard):
    out = []
    x = r.randint(0, 2)
    while x < W and len(out) < 6 + hard:
        w = r.choice(WID)
        if x + w > W:
            break
        out.append((x, w))
        x += w + (r.randint(1, 2) if r.random() < 0.5 + 0.2 * hard else r.randint(5, 10))
    return out


def facts(B):
    LS = [[[k for k, v in enumerate(B[i + 1]) if over(u, v)] if i < len(B) - 1 else []
           for u in B[i]] for i in range(len(B))]
    return LS, [[len(x) for x in row] for row in LS]


def vecs(B, D, gaps):
    # every per-line readout of the picture a player might try; "drip" is the true rule
    rr = range(len(B) - 1)
    LS, cnt = facts(B)
    lg = lambda i, j: D[i][j] == gaps[i]
    cov = lambda i, j: any(B[i][j][0] <= B[i + 1][k][0] and
                           B[i + 1][k][0] + B[i + 1][k][1] <= B[i][j][0] + B[i][j][1]
                           for k in LS[i][j])
    C = lambda f: tuple(sum(1 for j in range(len(B[i])) if f(i, j)) for i in rr)
    return {
        "drip": C(lambda i, j: lg(i, j) and cnt[i][j]),
        "reach": C(lg),
        "below": C(lambda i, j: cnt[i][j]),
        "gar": C(lambda i, j: 1),
        "short": C(lambda i, j: not lg(i, j)),
        "shortb": C(lambda i, j: not lg(i, j) and cnt[i][j]),
        "wide": C(lambda i, j: B[i][j][1] > 2),
        "cont": C(lambda i, j: lg(i, j) and cov(i, j)),
        "lw": C(lambda i, j: lg(i, j) and B[i][j][1] > 2),
        "ln": C(lambda i, j: lg(i, j) and B[i][j][1] < 3),
        "in": C(lambda i, j: lg(i, j) and cnt[i][j] and 0 < j < len(B[i]) - 1),
        "pairs": tuple(sum(cnt[i][j] for j in range(len(B[i])) if lg(i, j)) for i in rr),
        "wet": tuple(len({k for j in range(len(B[i])) if lg(i, j) for k in LS[i][j]})
                     for i in rr)}


def ok(v, d):
    return (v["drip"] == d
            and all(a > b for a, b in zip(v["reach"], d))
            and all(a > b for a, b in zip(v["below"], d))
            and all(v[k] != d for k in v if k not in ("drip", "reach", "below")))


def render(B, D, gaps, W, r, lets):
    f = r.choice("..,:")
    out = []
    for i, b in enumerate(B):
        rail = ["="] * W
        for x, w in b:
            rail[x] = rail[x + w - 1] = "v"
        rows = [[f] * W for _ in range(gaps[i])]
        for j, xw in enumerate(b):
            for k in range(xw[1]):
                for y in range(D[i][j]):
                    rows[y][xw[0] + k] = lets[i][j]
        out += ["".join(rail)] + ["".join(x) for x in rows]
    return "\n".join(out)


# the scorer itself: solve never ships a picture it has not verified
def check(c,s):
 w,g,n=c.split("/");L=s.strip().split("\n");B=[];E=set("=v")
 if set(L[0])-E or any(len(x)!=int(w)for x in L):return 0
 for x in L:
  if set(x)-E:B[-1]+=[{(*m.span(),m.group()[0])for m in re.finditer(r"([A-Z])\1*",x)}]
  else:B+=[[]]
 if[*map(len,B)]!=[*map(int,g)]or any(len(b[0])<2 or any(map(set.__sub__,b[1:],b))for b in B):return 0
 return int([sum(all(p in q for q in b)and any(p[0]<v and u<p[1]for u,v,z in B[i+1][0])for p in b[0])for i,b in enumerate(B[:-1])]==[*map(int,n)])


def solve(clue):
    w, g, n = clue.split("/")
    W = int(w)
    gaps = [int(c) for c in g]
    d = tuple(int(c) for c in n)
    R = len(gaps)
    r = random.Random(clue)
    for att in range(2500):
        B = [block(r, W, att > 250) for _ in gaps]
        if any(len(b) < 4 for b in B):
            continue
        LS, cnt = facts(B)
        S = set()
        good = True
        for i in range(R):
            pos = [j for j in range(len(B[i])) if cnt[i][j]]
            zer = [j for j in range(len(B[i])) if not cnt[i][j]]
            r.shuffle(pos)
            r.shuffle(zer)
            if i == R - 1:
                S |= {(i, j) for j in zer[:r.randint(1, len(zer))]} if zer else set()
                continue
            if len(pos) < d[i] + 1 or not zer:
                good = False
                break
            S |= {(i, j) for j in pos[:d[i]]} | {(i, j) for j in zer[:r.randint(1, len(zer))]}
        if not good:
            continue
        D = [[gaps[i] if (i, j) in S else r.randint(1, gaps[i] - 1)
              for j in range(len(b))] for i, b in enumerate(B)]
        if not ok(vecs(B, D, gaps), d):
            continue
        pal = r.sample(list("TSPJDCHV"), r.randint(3, 5))
        lets = []
        for b in B:
            row = []
            for _ in b:
                row.append(r.choice([x for x in pal if not row or x != row[-1]]))
            lets.append(row)
        if len({x for q in lets for x in q}) < 3:
            continue
        out = render(B, D, gaps, W, r, lets)
        if check(clue, out) == 1:
            return out
    return ""
